title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — learned man inconsistent: in alio peccare = imputation, then prior to it
pass_a_gloss: Placeus: the opponent will not hold together. He first made 'sin in another' mean the same as alien-sin imputation; now he splits them and puts in-another sinning before imputation as its cause. The shift from identity to priority undercuts his own prior paragraph.
pass_b_english: Next the learned man does not seem to himself to stand consistent enough. For he had said in the preceding paragraph that for someone to sin in another designates imputation by force of the word, and that to sin in another and for another's sin to be imputed are the same. Now he will have them to be diverse; and that to sin in another is prior to another's sin being imputed; and that this as the later, that as the prior and cause.
source_text: Deinde non videtur Vir doctus sibi satis constare. Dixerat enim paragrapho praecedente aliquem in alio peccare ex vi vocis designare imputationem, idemque esse in alio peccare ac peccatum alienum imputari. Nunc vult esse diversa; & prius esse peccare in alio, quam peccatum alienum imputari; hocque tanquam posterius, illud supponere, tanquam prius & causam.

choices.choice: in alio peccare first = imputation, then prior cause of it
